newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals weaker, vulnerable to drops.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals weaker, vulnerable to drops.

text.p: Precious metals were weaker on Friday morning and looked vulnerable to further easing due to a lack of buying interest, dealers said.
Gold fixed easier at $385.60 an ounce, compared to $386.00 on Thursday morning and afternoon.
Silver also lost ground on fund selling in New York after London closed, and platinum continued its week-long slide.
"The whole market is threatening to come down. There's just no interest at all," a dealer said.
Market sentiment remained bearish since U.S. missile strikes on Iraq earlier this week failed to translate into a rally.
If support at around $385 failed to hold, prices could easily drop to the next level around $383, dealers said.
"There's a feeling there may be producer buy-backs at $385 as well as dribs and drabs of physical buying," a dealer said.
"But the charts don't look good and the New York close was fairly weak so I don't think the $385 level will hold," he said.
But other dealers said recent plays in the options market suggested prices would remain in the $385-$390 range.
Options provide the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an instrument or commodity at a given price.
The market was keeping a close eye on U.S. economic data for signs of strong economic growth, and the effect on inflation.
The fear of higher inflation is traditionally bullish for gold. But many analysts say any positive effects were likely to be overridden by a bearish threat of a hike in U.S. interest rates.
Silver was indicated five cents lower at $5.15 an ounce.
"It looks very, very poorly. But there should be some support at $5.00-$5.05," a dealer said.
Platinum, which has been losing steam regularly over the past five days, was down $1.15 from Thursday's London close at $393.25. Palladium was off $0.50 at $125.00.
